## TL;DR

Updated the macOS Hub release workflow so a release tag still publishes `RepoOSHub.dmg` when every Apple notarization secret is absent. That path preserves the app build, bundle validation, DMG packaging, and mounted install checks, then records a warning and an explicit “Not notarized” job summary. A dry run with no credentials fails clearly because it did not exercise notarization. Partial credentials and all notarization, stapling, or verification errors remain fatal before upload. The workflow’s tag trigger no longer has a path filter that suppresses tag runs. Updated both Hub guides and the release runbook, corrected the Android asset-link claim, and added workflow-content coverage.

## Work and rationale

The release job already injected all six relevant secret values into the notarization step and had useful fail-closed logic for partial Apple ID and API-key credentials. The missing behavior was the all-empty case: it entered the Apple ID branch, failed because the required values were absent, and prevented an otherwise valid DMG from reaching upload. The new all-empty guard executes before `jq` or any notary calls. For an actual tag release it prints a GitHub Actions warning, appends a summary explaining that the checked DMG will be uploaded without a notarization ticket, then succeeds so the later upload can run. It only examines whether the injected values are empty; it never prints or writes a secret.

For dispatch dry runs, the no-credentials branch instead appends a “Notarization not exercised” summary and exits with an error. This preserves the meaning of a dry run as validation of the notarization pipeline; it cannot silently report success without having exercised it. The upload step retains its dry-run guard, and for credentialed runs it remains after the existing submission acceptance, ticket stapling, ticket validation, and Gatekeeper assessment. Existing checks still fail the job before upload on partial credentials or any notary, timeout, staple, or verification failure.

The `push` trigger used `branches` and `tags` together with `paths`. Path filters do not make sense for tag refs and can prevent expected tag workflow runs. I removed only the push path filter, retaining path-scoped pull-request builds and main-branch push behavior while allowing version tags to trigger the release job.

The macOS release runbook now describes both credential states and the release checklist tells maintainers what to verify in the job summary. The user installation guide explains that an unnotarized release needs the first-launch “Open Anyway” action, while a notarized release should not need that exception. The Android guide now accurately says the `latest/download` route selects the latest stable release and does not search older releases for an APK when the selected release has no such asset.

The workflow test asserts the tag trigger has no path filter, the empty-secret warning and summary are present, missing-credential dry runs fail explicitly, partial sets still have validation errors, the notarization gates remain, and upload follows those gates and is disabled for dry runs.

## Approaches tried

I first inspected the release workflow, its existing credential branches, the workflow-content test, and the relevant runbook sections. Rather than restructuring the working credentialed path, I added a narrow no-secrets branch before the existing notarization validation. This keeps the established credential behavior intact and makes the new exception visible at the workflow step and in the job summary.

The first required changed-path check found a formatting issue in the new test. I ran the repository formatter and reran the check. After identifying the dry-run type mismatch, I formatted again and ran the required check once more on the final tree. I also reviewed the edited workflow and documentation diff and searched for related stale claims about a latest-download fallback. During final review I noticed that `dry_run` is a boolean input while the pre-existing upload condition compared it to the string `'true'`. I changed the condition to a boolean comparison and extended the test to assert it, ensuring the no-publish guarantee is explicit in the workflow expression.

## Challenges and blockers

The repository’s Apple secret values and live macOS release environment were not inspected, and no real notarization submission or tag publication was run. Therefore this report makes no claim about live GitHub secret configuration, Apple acceptance, or an uploaded release artifact. The implemented branches and workflow assertions cover the intended behavior; actual notarization remains dependent on maintainers configuring complete credentials. No credentials or secret values were added, echoed, or committed.

The first check failed only at formatting; after formatting, the required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed, including remote changed-path tests, build, browser gate, user-docs build, local lint/format, UI smoke, and rendered contrast checks.

## Key learnings

An empty credential configuration needs an explicit policy branch before credential-set validation; otherwise the same “missing credentials” error conflates “not configured at all” with “partially configured,” even when those cases should have different release outcomes. Testing the empty state and the partial states separately protects that boundary. A dry run also needs a distinct no-credentials result, because succeeding without notarization would claim to have tested a gate that never ran. Finally, version-tag filters should not be combined with path filters when the requirement is that every matching pushed tag starts a release run.
